'''Desmond Ferguson''' (born July 22, 1977, in [[Lansing, Michigan]]) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and coach. He last played with the [[Halifax Rainmen]] of the [[Premier Basketball League|PBL]].<ref>[http://www.rainmenbasketball.ca/component/option,com_zoo/Itemid,31/layout,category/view,category/ Halifax Rainmen roster] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324165450/http://www.rainmenbasketball.ca/component/option,com_zoo/Itemid,31/layout,category/view,category |date=March 24, 2016 }}. Retrieved on December 20, 2009.</ref> He attended and played [[college basketball]] for the [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri Tigers]] as a freshman and his last three seasons with the [[Detroit Mercy Titans men's basketball|Detroit Mercy Titans]].

He was signed by the [[National Basketball Association]]'s [[Portland Trail Blazers]] to a 10-day contract in March 2004,<ref>[http://www.hoopshype.com/general_managers/john_nash.htm HoopsHype – NBA General Managers - John Nash<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> and appeared in seven games with them during the [[2003–04 NBA season]]. He was later taken by the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] during the [[2004 NBA expansion draft]] and was waived sometime before the season began. Ferguson only played in the NBA for two weeks, with his final game ever being on April 14, 2004, in a 105–104 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers. The game went to double overtime, but Ferguson only played for {{frac|3|1|2}} minutes total and recorded 3 points.

Ferguson was a two-time All-[[Continental Basketball Association]] (CBA) First Team selection in 2007 and 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=Desmond Ferguson minor league basketball statistics |url=https://www.statscrew.com/minorbasketball/stats/p-fergudes001 |website=Stats Crew |access-date=June 21, 2021}}</ref>

Ferguson retired from playing in 2011, becoming a high school coach at his alma mater, [[Everett High School (Michigan)|Everett High School]] in Lansing. He left that post in 2017 to focus on his business interests.<ref>{{cite news |last1= Couch |first1= Graham |title= Desmond Ferguson steps down after 5 years at Everett |url= https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/05/30/desmond-ferguson-steps-down-everett/356719001/ |accessdate=November 24, 2019 |work=[[Lansing State Journal]] |date=May 30, 2017}}</ref>
